key_insight: Embedding random Fourier features into a PINN reduces spectral bias, enabling much better resolution of sharp elastic-plastic gradients and plastic zones in non-associative Mohr-Coulomb geomaterials.
engineering_relevance: The method offers a faster, mesh-free surrogate for geotechnical elasto-plastic analysis that can reduce reliance on costly FEM incremental-iterative solves while preserving physics consistency.
method: Random Fourier feature mapping is added to the PINN input layer to better represent high-frequency stress/displacement fields.
A multi-objective loss enforces equilibrium, constitutive laws, and KKT conditions using FEM data.
Strain-adaptive sampling focuses training points near evolving plastic regions and failure boundaries.
evidence_signal: Across three benchmark cases, FF-PINN reduced errors by up to about 66% in displacement and 27% in stress, reproduced plastic zone geometry more faithfully than a conventional PINN, and converged in roughly half the training epochs.
watch_item: Performance is validated against specific benchmark cases and FEM data, so transfer to more complex 3D problems or strongly different loading/soil conditions may require retuning the feature mapping and loss weights.
paper_title: Fourier Feature Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Elasto-Plastic Analysis of Geomaterials with a Non-Associative Mohr-Coulomb Model
